clue.text: Study for one with his head in the clouds

definitions.text: Study for one with his head in the clouds

parts.words: Study for one with his head in the clouds
parts.note: a daydreamer has his head in the clouds, but read literally this is the science a meteorologist pursues by studying the sky

explanation.surface: A course of study suited to a dreamy, absent-minded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head in the clouds' usually means absent-minded; here it is meant literally, the subject being the scientific study of clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek nephos means cloud, so this is the branch of meteorology that studies cloud formation.

clue.text: Leading lady right as always

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, leads all ladies in the Genesis story

explanation.surface: A star actress who is always correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a stage star, but it is Eve, the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning at all times, as in 'for ever'.

clue.text: The patisserie's best seller?

parts.note: things that sell quickly are said to sell like ..., so the pastry shop's top line is literally that baked item

explanation.surface: Which item flies off the shelves at a cake shop?
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'selling like hot cakes' means selling fast; the clue takes it literally for a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in great demand is called this, from the idiom about rapid sales.

clue.text: Calls to watch television

definitions.meaning: to drop by briefly on someone, pay a visit
informally, to tune in and view a broadcast

explanation.surface: Phoning someone to suggest viewing a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both paying a short visit and tuning in as a viewer.

clue.text: Silver found in Georgia? Must be slightly crazy

indicators.note: the silver is discovered placed within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Anyone claiming to have struck silver in Georgia must be a little mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals a container: the metal sits inside the state's abbreviation, and the question mark warns that 'Georgia' is the US state rather than the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for dotty, senile or infatuated, i.e. a bit mad.

clue.text: Holding a personal conversation?

parts.note: a conversation that is entirely personal involves only one person, speaking alone to himself as an actor does on stage

explanation.surface: Having a private chat with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal conversation' suggests a private talk between two; read literally, it is one person talking to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking one's thoughts aloud alone, as Hamlet does in 'To be or not to be'.

clue.text: First bid and last offer

definitions.meaning: at an auction, the opening figure at which bidding begins
in horse racing, the final odds offered by bookmakers when the race begins

explanation.surface: An auction in which the opening bid is also the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an auction's opening price and also a racehorse's final odds, the SP of betting.

clue.text: Tippler's speculations about signing the pledge?

definitions.text: Tippler's speculations about signing the pledge?

parts.words: Tippler's speculations about signing the pledge?
parts.note: a drinker considering a vow of abstinence is literally thinking about being sober, and the phrase also means calm reflection

explanation.surface: A drinker wondering whether to swear off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signing the pledge' means promising to give up drink; the phrase for calm, considered reflection is read literally as a drinker's thoughts about sobriety.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means considered, rational reflection, here literally reflections on staying off drink.

clue.text: Angler who is no fool, apparently

definitions.text: Angler who is no fool, apparently

parts.words: Angler who is no fool, apparently
parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or knowing, so an angler with that word before his title appears to be shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: The angler uses artificial flies; but 'fly' is also British slang for streetwise, so the name seems to say he is no fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler who casts artificial flies as bait for trout or salmon.

clue.text: Error is evident in an abstainer, making him a dangerous character

indicators.note: the mistake and the word is are seen sitting inside the abstainer

parts.note: TT is short for teetotal, a teetotaller
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An abstainer's mistake turns him into a menace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is evident in' signals a container; TT, for teetotal, is the crossword's usual abstainer, and here it splits to hold the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone using violence to intimidate for political ends is a dangerous person.

clue.text: Life style given to navigator Ericson

indicators.note: the letters of the word are given a new style, rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A biography in the manner of the Norse explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' rearranges LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse explorer Leif Erikson reportedly reached North America around 1000 AD.

clue.text: Delay a function on the piano initially

indicators.note: the musical abbreviation is to be placed first, before the other pieces

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
a function is a use or purpose

explanation.surface: Postponing a recital: a piano function put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' puts P (piano, soft) before A and USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stop or hesitation is a delay; as a verb, to wait briefly.

clue.text: Idiom derived from Lowlanders earlier on

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A dialect that Scottish Lowlanders spoke in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derived from' points to the letters inside lowlandERS Earlier. The surface's Lowlanders spoke Scots, a cousin of Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for Gaelic, a language or idiom in the sense of a form of speech.

clue.text: Cordial plant with a relative sounding name

indicators.note: the word for the relative is heard rather than spelt, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a niece is a relative, your sibling's daughter

explanation.surface: A plant with a family-sounding name used in liqueurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' says A NIECE is heard, and that sounds like the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Its seeds flavour liqueurs such as anisette, so it is a plant used in cordials.

clue.text: Guy aboard is about right to drift off

indicators.note: the rope goes around the abbreviation, containing it

parts.note: a guy is a supporting rope; on a ship such a rope is a stay

explanation.surface: A man on a ship wanders off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is a guy rope; on board ship that is a STAY. 'is about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander or drift away from where one should be.

clue.text: Ruffle with impatient movements

definitions.meaning: a frill or ornamental strip on a skirt
an angry, exaggerated sweep of the body when storming off

explanation.surface: Someone ruffled who moves about impatiently.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a dress frill and a huffy, flamboyant exit.

clue.text: Portrait painter I chat easily about

indicators.note: the chatting goes around the letter, surrounding it

parts.note: to natter is to chat casually and at length

explanation.surface: A portrait artist who chats freely with sitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside NATTER. Jean-Marc Nattier was an 18th-century French portraitist at the court of Louis XV.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Marc Nattier was a French artist famed for portraits of court ladies.

clue.text: Brings the speech to a close?

definitions.text: Brings the speech to a close?

parts.words: Brings the speech to a close?
parts.note: suggests a speaker winding up an address, but means silencing someone or stopping one's own talk

explanation.surface: A speaker concluding an address.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a formal end to an oration; the answer is the blunt phrase for falling, or making someone fall, silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means stops talking or silences another person.

clue.text: Patronised pupil peer got to develop

indicators.note: the letters are made to develop into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman's favoured student who has grown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to develop' rearranges PEER and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person guided and sponsored by an influential mentor.

clue.text: Brag about new-laid raw eggs

indicators.note: the eggs are laid out anew, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Boasting about freshly laid uncooked eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-laid' rearranges RAW EGGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to strut and boast, a synonym of boasting.

clue.text: Poet lacking a saving grace?

definitions.meaning: Stephen ..., English poet of the 1930s generation
someone without the virtue of thrift, a person who does not save money

explanation.surface: A poet with no redeeming quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving grace' means a redeeming feature; read literally it is the habit of saving money, which a big spender lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was a 20th-century English poet; and one who spends freely does not save.

clue.text: Yes, one may make it without exertion

definitions.text: Yes, one may make it without exertion

parts.words: Yes, one may make it without exertion
parts.note: the agreement that something can be achieved effortlessly hints at cash gained with no hard work

explanation.surface: Agreeing that something can be done effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make it' looks like succeeding; read as making cash, it describes income gained for little work.
explanation.definitionFit: Money acquired with little effort or by dubious means.

clue.text: See 21
There's risk involved with this weapon

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up, involved in a new order

explanation.surface: This weapon is dangerous to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: Race with no competitors in Algeria

parts.note: nobody taking part is nil, the letter O
to race is to run; ran is its past

explanation.surface: An uncontested race held in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No competitors' gives O, nought, and 'race' gives RAN: 'O ran', nobody ran. The definition 'in Algeria' stands for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: A major port city on Algeria's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Good song for her opposite number one hears

indicators.note: the word is heard, not spelt, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: the masculine counterpart of the pronoun her is him

explanation.surface: A fine song for her counterpart, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' says HIM, the male opposite of 'her', is said aloud. 'Good song' means a sacred song, the Good Book sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious song of praise sung in church.

clue.text: Not the kind of thing a Quaker would take part in, presumably

definitions.text: Not the kind of thing a Quaker would take part in, presumably

parts.words: Not the kind of thing a Quaker would take part in, presumably
parts.note: Quakers belong to the Society of Friends, so a hostile deed would literally be unsuited to a Friend

explanation.surface: Something a pacifist Quaker would avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: Quakers form the Religious Society of Friends; the diplomatic phrase for a hostile move is read as an act unfitting for a Friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic term for a hostile action by one state against another.

clue.text: Grenadine can be so sweetly attractive

indicators.note: the letters can be turned into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Pomegranate syrup is so charmingly sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges GRENADINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming and lovable, inspiring affection.
